paragraphs.notes: Bold heading opening the claims section, first inked body line of the page. No paragraph marker and no claim number. The words are bold, the colon appears not to be.

paragraphs.zh: 1. A process for preparation of mesotrione of formula (I), which comprises: (i) oxidizing2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) using an oxidant in presence of ruthenium oxide as a catalyst, to produce 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III); (ii) reacting NMSBA of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione to produce an enol ester of formula (II); and (iii) converting the enol ester of formula (II) to mesotrione of formula (I)
paragraphs.en: 1. A process for preparation of mesotrione of formula (I), which comprises: (i) oxidizing2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) using an oxidant in presence of ruthenium oxide as a catalyst, to produce 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III); (ii) reacting NMSBA of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione to produce an enol ester of formula (II); and (iii) converting the enol ester of formula (II) to mesotrione of formula (I)
paragraphs.notes: Claim 1. Independent claim: it refers back to no other claim. It is the only independent claim on this page. marker is null because claims carry their own arabic numbering rather than a bracketed paragraph number; the printed claim number '1.' is kept at the start of the text. Claim 1 is one entry here, with its three sub-clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) joined by single spaces, because the page prints them as indented continuations of the one claim; on the page a reaction scheme is printed between (i) and (ii), another between (ii) and (iii), and a third after (iii), and those three are drawings[0], drawings[1] and drawings[2] in that order. Transcription oddities kept exactly as printed: 'oxidizing2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl' has no space after 'oxidizing'; the same sentence spells the moiety two ways, 'methylsulfonyl' with an f for NMST and 'methylsulphonyl' with a ph for NMSBA, which is the pattern brief section 8 describes; sub-clause (iii) ends with no punctuation at all, no full stop and no semicolon, so claim 1 as printed has no terminal period. Claim 1 is complete on this page: it is followed by claim 2, also complete here. Claim 1 contains no quantity, no concentration, no temperature, no time, no pressure and no molar ratio; the only numerals in it are the roman formula numbers (I) to (IV) and the locants in the chemical names, '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl', '2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl' and '1,3-cyclohexanedione'.

paragraphs.zh: 2. The process for preparation of mesotrione as claimed in claim 1, wherein the NMST of formula (IV) is oxidized using sodium hypochloritein presence of ruthenium oxide.
paragraphs.en: 2. The process for preparation of mesotrione as claimed in claim 1, wherein the NMST of formula (IV) is oxidized using sodium hypochloritein presence of ruthenium oxide.
paragraphs.notes: Claim 2. Dependent claim: it refers back to claim 1 by the words 'as claimed in claim 1', and narrows step (i) by naming the oxidant. marker is null for the reason given on claim 1; the printed claim number '2.' is kept at the start of the text. Printing oddity kept as printed: 'sodium hypochloritein presence' has no space between 'hypochlorite' and 'in'. Claim 2 is complete on this page, ending in a full stop, and it is the last inked text on the page; the claims continue with claim 3 on p20. Claim 2 gives no quantity, no concentration and no molar ratio, only the identity of the oxidant.

drawings.notes: Scheme for step (i) of claim 1, printed between sub-clause (i) and sub-clause (ii) of claim 1. Nothing is written below the arrow; the only arrow label is the single string 'Oxidant / RuO2' set above it, recorded as one reagent string because that is how it is printed, with a slash and no separation of oxidant from catalyst. The printed structure labels are 'Formula IV' and 'Formula III', with no parentheses, whereas the claim text beside them writes 'formula (IV)' and 'formula (III)' with parentheses; both forms kept as printed. Every ring position was counted off the drawn hexagon vertices at 5x to 6x magnification, not inferred from the names. The ink of both structures is broken dotted throughout and the subscript 2 of SO2 on Formula III degrades far enough to look like a 7 at page scale; read as 2 at magnification and from the matching label on Formula IV. The arrow is a degraded solid line with one solid arrowhead, not a dashed arrow, per brief section 9. Kekule double bonds are drawn on both rings in a valid alternating pattern.

drawings.notes: Scheme for step (ii) of claim 1, printed between sub-clause (ii) and sub-clause (iii) of claim 1. The arrow is completely bare: nothing is written above it and nothing below it, so no coupling agent, base, solvent or temperature is given anywhere in this scheme, and the claim text beside it gives none either. The middle reactant carries no printed label of its own; the claim text names it 1,3-cyclohexanedione and the drawn 1,3 relationship agrees, so nothing is recorded in discrepancies. The enol ester regiochemistry was read off the drawing: the ester oxygen sits on the ring carbon that carries the C=C, and the ketone sits two bonds round the ring from it. The printed label is 'Formula II', no parentheses, against 'formula (II)' in the claim text. Ink is broken dotted throughout; the H3C-SO2 label on Formula II is the poorest glyph group on the page and was resolved at 6x.

drawings.notes: Scheme for step (iii) of claim 1, the last thing printed before claim 2. The arrow is bare, nothing above and nothing below, and sub-clause (iii) says only 'converting', so the page names no catalyst, base, solvent, temperature or time for this step at all. The two drawn structures are isomers of one another, C14H13NO7S each, which is consistent with the step being a rearrangement of the enol ester rather than an addition or a loss; that is a check on the transcription, not something the page says. Ring positions counted off the drawn vertices at 6x: on Formula I's benzene the hexagon has a vertical left edge and a vertical right edge, the exocyclic carbonyl leaves the upper-right vertex, NO2 sits on the top vertex adjacent to it, and the S sits on the lower-left vertex, which is the vertex diagonally opposite the carbonyl and therefore C4. Printed labels are 'Formula II' and 'Formula I', no parentheses. The top of the Formula II cyclohexenone ring, including its ketone O, is not clipped, but it sits tight under the sub-clause (iii) text line above it and had to be read in a separate crop.

discrepancies.what: The oxidant is named on the page but not on the scheme that depicts the oxidation.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The step (i) arrow carries the single label 'Oxidant / RuO2' above it and nothing below it, naming no specific oxidant and joining the oxidant and the ruthenium oxide with a slash as though they were one reagent entry.
discrepancies.text_says: Claim 1 (i) distinguishes them, 'using an oxidant in presence of ruthenium oxide as a catalyst', and claim 2 on the same page names the oxidant as sodium hypochlorite. Recorded rather than resolved: claim 1 is deliberately generic, so this may be drafting intent rather than an error, but a later pass reading 'Oxidant / RuO2' as one reagent string would lose the catalyst distinction.

discrepancies.what: The claimed route has three steps and no benzoyl chloride, which is one step fewer than the route the vision brief describes.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The three schemes on this page run Formula IV to Formula III to Formula II to Formula I, that is NMST to NMSBA to the enol ester to mesotrione. No acid chloride is drawn anywhere on the page.
discrepancies.text_says: Claim 1 matches the drawings: NMSBA of formula (III) reacts directly with 1,3-cyclohexanedione. Brief section 8 states the route runs NMST to NMSBA to NMSBC to mesotrione, with NMSBC being the benzoyl chloride. On this page NMSBC is neither drawn, named, nor abbreviated. Recorded here rather than silently reconciled: either the description elsewhere carries a benzoyl chloride variant that claim 1 does not claim, or the brief is wrong about the route.
